notes: Reader B, part 2: rows with sample_index 40 through 79. Method: for every row I rendered the context area of the original PDF page from the geometry in selection.json (context, glyph and field boxes) at several scales with PyMuPDF (raster pixels only), read the numbered line and its classification field, and compared each unit with the position-chart cards (candidate sets are listed per unit with the chart location). Crop judgments used the proposed glyph box against connected ink components in a higher-resolution render of the page: a crop is marked incorrect when it contains ink of a neighbouring row or field, or cuts off drawing or underline ink of the target. Conventions applied: units are listed in visual left-to-right order; underline presence is recorded per unit and 'strict_candidate_codes' include the underline state, while 'shape_only_candidate_codes' also list the underlined or plain partner codes. Coincident cards (8/764, 9/765, 10/766, 12/767, 501/768, 543/769, 205/206/208, 435/436, 144/244) are kept as sets. Underlines lie about 1 pt below the glyph line and span the sign cell; a dash line between two rows belongs to the upper row. Hatched patches (597/598 and partners): the right-edge variant (598) was chosen where the patch ink ended about 2 pt before the next sign's cell start (rows 53, 55, 77, 78 first unit); the left-edge variant (597) was chosen where the patch ink began about 1.5 pt after the previous sign's ink (rows 78 last unit, 79). In row 53 the patch position was also compared with the left cell origin of the page column (other rows start at about 351 pt, the patch at 359.5 pt). Printed digits: the typeface sometimes draws the digit 1 like an i (a stroke with a dot and no flag); these were read as 1 (rows 44, 46, 47, 49, 52, 60, 71, 75, 79). The classification literal keeps a blank third position as a space where printed (for example '11 40'). Row 48 prints the single digit 5 as its number. Hardest judgments: row 52 first unit (diamond with a stalk and hand-shaped patch, closest card 166 but the stalk differs); row 47 sixth unit (tick plus bent stroke, read as the single card 154); row 54 (144/244 label uncertainty kept as a set); the Y signs with a long centre prong in rows 43, 66 and 77 (card 126, with 151 as the underlined partner); the dot in row 64's fourth unit (read as a speck, 204, not the one-tick 205); and the 597/598 choices above. Crop findings: rows 44, 48, 55, 58 and 66 include a thin top strip of the next row's glyphs at the bottom edge of the box; rows 76 and 77 cut off the last unit (and, in 77, its underline) at the right edge and their field boxes overlap the drawing. Exposure: I did not open predictions, the frame, freeze files, pipeline outputs, other readers' folders, evaluation or repair references, or the PDF text layer, and I saw none of them. My own scratch folder was used for renders and helper scripts and was deleted at the end. A first attempt to append a row to a helper file hung on a stray shell command and was stopped; it touched nothing outside my scratch folder.
